summary: Dashboard variable binding strips trace_id from generated 'Open Trace' URLs causing 404s
description: Issue summary: When users view a dashboard with a variable-driven panel that surfaces recent requests, the panel renders an 'Open Trace' link per row. For dashboards where the panel query uses a templated variable (e.g., ${session_id} or ${request_id}), the rendering pipeline is stripping the trace_id query parameter from the constructed URL. Impact: clicking 'Open Trace' results in a 404 on the tracing service UI for ~60% of rows. This prevents customers from drilling into traces from dashboards, blocking incident investigations and SRE workflows. Environment: Production (us-east), Redwood Console v5.4.2, tracing-service v2.11. Steps to reproduce: 1) Login to Redwood Console as a customer user for Acme Financial (dedicated). 2) Open saved dashboard "Payments — Live Overview" with timeframe Last 30m. 3) Locate the panel "Recent API requests" which uses a dashboard variable ${recent_request_id}. 4) Click the 'Open Trace' link in any row. Observed behavior: The browser navigates to /tracing/trace?id=<blank> or to /tracing/trace with id equal to the row's request_id rather than the expected trace_id. Tracing UI shows "Trace not found" (404). Expected behavior: Each 'Open Trace' link should include the full trace_id token and route directly to the corresponding trace in the tracing UI. Logs/artifacts: - Console network capture attached to support ticket (request_capture_2026-03-10.har) shows the panel row payload includes trace_id in the backend response but the client-side link href omits it. - Dashboard rendering trace in console logs: panelRenderer->bindVariables shows substitution "request_id=abc123" then later linkBuilder logs "trace_id=" (empty). Investigation notes: - Reproduced in customer prod tenant and in internal staging with dedicated config. - Backend API (dashboards/v1/panels/data) returns rows with a trace_id field present. - The template variable substitution code in dashboard-renderer on the client appears to incorrectly pick the last bound variable (session_id) instead of the trace_id field when building query params for trace links. - Possible regression introduced during recent variable-escape patch (PR #4821). - No signs of authentication/permissions blocking (auth headers present and tracing service returns 200 for direct hits when correct id is provided). Customer impact: High — prevents drilldowns during incidents and increases time-to-resolution for on-call. Temporary workaround: Use the tracing search with the request_id or manually paste trace_id (if available) into tracing UI. A more accessible workaround is to export panel CSV and open traces by id. Next steps / proposed fix: 1) Patch client linkBuilder in dashboard-renderer to explicitly prefer trace_id field when present; add unit tests. 2) Backport fix to v5.4.x hotfix branch and release patch. 3) Run quick canary on staging and deploy to us-east. 4) Notify affected customers and add a console banner while fix is rolling out. Time estimates: patch + unit tests ~4-6 hours, hotfix release ~2 hours, staged rollout ~1-2 hours.
